ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in the Sahel changed by +0.045 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.015 to +0.086), which is statistically significant (p = 0.0015). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.110 mm/day.

ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in the Sahel changed by +0.0009 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.0002 to +0.0024), which is statistically significant (p = 0.0084). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.0023 mm/day.

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in the Sahel shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.15): the estimate is +0.014 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.005 to +0.040). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
